title: Indeterministic laws leave room for a mental influence consistent with physics

statements.text: If physical laws are deterministic, any interference from outside breaks them. If they are indeterministic, as quantum theory seems to say, an interference may produce a result of nonzero probability and so be consistent with the laws. Eccles, with Popper, argued that the brain is so finely tuned that minute variations could have large effects.

sources.quote: But if they are indeterministic, interference might produce a result that has a probability greater than zero, and so be consistent with the laws.
Others argue that the structure of the brain is so finely tuned that minute variations could have macroscopic effects
